name: Model-based RL with Learned World Model (DreamerV3-style)
key_paper: Hafner, D., Lillicrap, T., Norouzi, M., & Ba, J. (2023). Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models. arXiv:2301.04104. Nature 2025 (extended); core predecessor: Hafner et al. (2020) Dream to Control, ICLR 2020; DreamerV2: Hafner et al. (2021) Mastering Atari with Discrete World Models, ICLR 2021.
algorithm_description: DreamerV3 learns a latent world model (RSSM — Recurrent State Space Model) from historical observations, then trains an Actor-Critic entirely inside imagined rollouts generated by that world model — never needing additional real environment interactions beyond the initial dataset. The world model consists of three components: an encoder that maps observations to latent states, a recurrent dynamics model (GRU-based) that predicts next latent states, and a decoder that reconstructs observations from latent states for self-supervised training. Once the world model is trained on real data, the actor and critic are trained using imagined multi-step trajectories generated by unrolling the dynamics model forward in latent space. Returns are computed using a lambda-return over imagined trajectories, and the critic is trained to match these returns. DreamerV3 introduces symlog (symmetric log) transformation of rewards and returns, fixed normalized KL balancing, and free bits to stabilize world model training across highly varied reward scales, making it robust without domain-specific tuning.
action_space_handling: Standard DreamerV3 handles discrete scalar actions (one-hot Categorical) or continuous actions (diagonal Gaussian) natively. The actor outputs a distribution over actions; for discrete domains, this is a Categorical over a flat action index. For combinatorial set actions (choose k from N), DreamerV3 requires non-trivial adaptation: the actor must either (1) output N independent Bernoulli logits sampled with straight-through gradients to form a multi-hot vector, (2) use an autoregressive factored actor that generates one number at a time conditioned on previous selections, or (3) use Gumbel-top-k to sample exactly k items jointly. Imagined rollouts in the world model must be conditioned on whichever action representation is chosen, so the dynamics model must accept multi-hot or sequential action inputs. This is a significant adaptation from the standard single-index discrete action space.
how_combinatorial_output_is_formed: DreamerV3 does not natively form combinatorial outputs. For a k-of-N lottery adaptation, two practical approaches exist: (1) Autoregressive actor in latent space — at each imagined step, the actor generates one number at a time (k sequential sub-steps per play), masking already-selected indices in the logits to enforce distinct selection; the world model dynamics are unrolled k times per play with the mask evolving. (2) Multi-hot straight-through actor — the actor outputs N Bernoulli logits; during imagination, the top-k indices are selected deterministically for the world model dynamics (straight-through gradient), and during inference, stochastic sampling yields diverse plays. The world model's RSSM must receive the action encoding at each imagination step, so the action embedding dimension is set to N (ball pool size) for multi-hot encoding or 1 for autoregressive index encoding.
sequential_generation_strategy: DreamerV3 itself is inherently sequential in the temporal (draw-to-draw) direction — the RSSM GRU maintains a hidden state across time steps representing the history of draws. Within a single play generation, the strategy depends on the adaptation chosen: (1) Multi-hot (joint) strategy: all k numbers are determined simultaneously from a single actor forward pass — inter-number correlations cannot be modeled, but imagination steps are short and training is stable. (2) Autoregressive strategy: k sequential sub-steps per play, each conditioned on prior selections via masking — captures correlations between selected numbers but requires k-times more imagination steps and increases the risk of world model compounding errors over the longer imagined sequence. For the lottery-nn project, the multi-hot joint strategy is preferred given the short imagination horizon (1-5 plays) and the added complexity cost of autoregressive unrolling inside the latent world model.
gradient_estimator_type: DreamerV3 uses reparameterization gradients throughout the world model (straight-through for discrete latents via the RSSM categorical bottleneck), avoiding high-variance REINFORCE estimators. For the actor trained inside the world model imagination: (1) Continuous actions: reparameterization (standard Gaussian path gradient). (2) Discrete actions: straight-through estimator through the Categorical sample, enabling low-variance backpropagation through the imagined trajectory. For multi-hot combinatorial actions, straight-through through the top-k selection is the natural extension (treating the binary mask as a discrete variable with straight-through gradient). This is a significant advantage over REINFORCE-based methods on small data: reparameterization/straight-through gradients have dramatically lower variance than score-function estimators, meaning less data is needed to get a useful gradient signal.
combinatorial_constraint_enforcement: DreamerV3 does not natively enforce combinatorial constraints. For lottery adaptation: (1) Autoregressive masking — the actor generates k numbers sequentially inside the imagination loop, masking already-chosen indices to -inf before each Categorical sample; this is the cleanest approach and guarantees exactly k distinct selections. (2) Straight-through top-k — the actor outputs N logits; the forward pass uses hard top-k selection (exactly k ones, N-k zeros) and the backward pass uses straight-through to treat this as differentiable; guarantees k distinct items, no rejection sampling needed. (3) Post-hoc rejection sampling — sample N independent Bernoulli draws and reject/resample until exactly k are selected; simple but introduces bias in the imagination dynamics (the world model sees variable-length action vectors). Approach (2) is most compatible with the DreamerV3 imagination loop structure.
sample_efficiency_rating: high. The core value proposition of DreamerV3 over model-free RL is extreme sample efficiency: by learning a world model and training the Actor-Critic on imagined rollouts, DreamerV3 can extract far more learning signal from a small fixed dataset than model-free methods that require fresh real interactions. In the lottery-nn context, 100-200 historical draws can be used to train a world model that then generates thousands of imagined draw sequences for Actor-Critic training — effectively amplifying the dataset. DreamerV3's symlog reward normalization and free bits KL regularization make it robust to sparse and skewed rewards. Published results show DreamerV3 achieves strong performance with 200K environment steps on Atari (vs. 40M for model-free PPO), a 200x sample advantage. However, this advantage assumes the world model generalizes accurately — with only 100-200 draws, world model accuracy is uncertain, and compounding model errors in imagined rollouts may undermine the sample efficiency gain.
regularization_built_in: DreamerV3 has rich built-in regularization: (1) KL balancing — the RSSM is trained with a balanced KL loss (0.8 * KL(stop_grad(posterior) || prior) + 0.2 * KL(posterior || stop_grad(prior))), preventing the posterior from collapsing. (2) Free bits — KL terms below a threshold (1 bit per dim) are not penalized, preventing the model from wasting capacity on trivial structure. (3) Symlog transformation — symmetric log scaling of inputs and targets compresses extreme reward values and stabilizes training across reward scales. (4) Lambda returns — the lambda-return mixes n-step and Monte Carlo returns, providing a bias-variance tradeoff. (5) Actor entropy regularizer — an entropy bonus discourages premature policy collapse. (6) World model reconstruction loss provides implicit regularization by requiring the latent state to be predictive of the next observation, preventing the dynamics model from memorizing noise.
known_failure_modes_on_small_data: Several failure modes are specifically relevant for n < 200: (1) World model hallucination — with very few training draws, the RSSM learns a poor dynamics model that generates unrealistic imagined sequences; the Actor-Critic then optimizes for these hallucinated dynamics rather than the true distribution, leading to plays that look good in imagination but perform no better than random in reality. (2) KL collapse — with insufficient data, the RSSM posterior may collapse to the prior, meaning the world model ignores observations and imagines random sequences regardless of the actual draw history. (3) Compounding model errors — even a small per-step world model error (5-10%) compounds exponentially over long imagined rollouts; for k=7 autoregressive steps, this can render imagined plays completely unreliable. (4) Overfitting of the world model — the RSSM can memorize the 100-200 draws without generalizing, acting as a lookup table rather than a generative model. (5) Mode collapse in imagination — the world model may generate a narrow set of imagined futures, causing the Actor-Critic to converge on a single dominant play set with no diversity.
data_regime_evidence: DreamerV3 has been validated primarily on tasks with thousands to millions of environment interactions, not on static datasets of < 200 samples. Key evidence: (1) minimum_training_samples_tested: The DreamerV3 paper (Hafner et al. 2023) reports results starting from 200K environment steps on Atari, 1M steps on continuous control; the smallest reported data regime is DreamerV2 on Crafter with ~100 unique game states, but these involve online interaction not static offline data. No published DreamerV3 evaluation on a fixed offline dataset of 100-200 samples exists. (2) performance_degradation_curve: [uncertain] — no published curve for DreamerV3 performance vs. dataset size in the 50-200 range. World model-based methods generally degrade more gracefully than model-free methods as data shrinks (because imagination amplifies signal), but the crossover point and degradation rate for n < 200 are not characterized in published literature. (3) comparison_baseline: In DreamerV3's paper benchmarks, it outperforms model-free PPO by 10-200x in sample efficiency on continuous control and Atari, but comparisons are for online settings. Offline adaptation (train world model on fixed historical data, then imagine) has been studied in MBPO (Janner et al. 2019, NeurIPS) and MOPO (Yu et al. 2020, NeurIPS) for continuous control, with demonstrated improvements over offline model-free methods at n=1000-5000 transitions — still well above the lottery-nn regime.
convergence_guarantees_small_n: [uncertain] DreamerV3 has no published finite-sample convergence guarantees for small offline datasets. Theoretical analysis of RSSM-based world models focuses on asymptotic expressiveness (Hafner et al. 2019 theoretical appendices) and does not provide PAC-style bounds. Related offline model-based RL theory (Kidambi et al. 2020, MOPO; Yu et al. 2021, COMBO) provides pessimistic bounds on the offline policy performance gap in terms of world model estimation error, but these bounds are loose and require n >> 200. In practice, DreamerV3 convergence on very small fixed datasets is expected to be slow and unreliable: the world model must learn draw-to-draw dynamics from only 100-200 transitions, which is insufficient to estimate a reliable latent dynamics model. Empirical convergence in this regime is not documented and would require project-specific experimentation.
reward_distribution_handling: DreamerV3 has the strongest reward distribution handling of any standard RL algorithm, specifically designed for reward scale robustness: (1) Symlog reward transformation — all rewards are passed through symlog(x) = sign(x) * ln(|x| + 1) before training, compressing extreme values and normalizing the 95% zero-reward / 5% positive-reward lottery distribution without manual scaling. (2) Two-hot encoding of returns — the critic models returns as a two-hot distribution over a fixed set of return buckets rather than a scalar, which is equivalent to distributional RL (analogous to C51) and captures the full return distribution including rare high-reward events. (3) Lambda returns with symlog targets — the return target uses lambda=0.95 mixing, providing stable multi-step return estimates. (4) Free bits KL — prevents the world model from collapsing on zero-reward sequences (which dominate a lottery dataset). For lottery sparse rewards (95% zero hits), symlog effectively shrinks the zero-reward mass and amplifies the gradient signal from the rare non-zero draws. Minimum draws for stable world model training: empirically estimated at 500+ real draws for DreamerV3 to learn a reliable dynamics model; 100-200 draws may yield an unstable world model that limits downstream Actor-Critic quality.
credit_assignment_granularity: DreamerV3 operates at the episode/trajectory level for credit assignment — the imagined rollout assigns returns to the actor based on cumulative imagined reward. In the lottery context, each draw constitutes a single timestep with one scalar reward (play-level credit). Number-level (semi-bandit) credit assignment is not natively supported but can be implemented by: (1) decomposing the reward into per-number hit signals (k separate binary rewards, one per ball) and training k separate reward models inside the world model; (2) using a shaped reward function (hits / k) that remains play-level but encodes partial information. The world model's reward predictor can learn to predict shaped hit-count rewards (0-7/7) from latent states, which provides richer gradient signal than binary win/loss during imagination. For lottery-nn, using shaped reward = num_hits / k is strongly recommended to make the world model's reward predictor learnable from the sparse hit distribution.
diversity_mechanism: DreamerV3 maintains play diversity through: (1) Actor entropy regularizer — an entropy term is added to the actor's imagined objective, penalizing deterministic policies and encouraging exploration of the number space. (2) Stochastic world model — the RSSM's stochastic latent state (Categorical distribution per step) introduces randomness into imagined trajectories, naturally generating diverse imagined histories that train the actor on varied scenarios. (3) Temperature sampling at inference — actor logits can be scaled by temperature T > 1 to increase sampling diversity when generating the final play recommendations. (4) World model imagination diversity — because the world model samples from a learned stochastic dynamics, different imagination rollouts diverge even from the same starting state, exposing the actor to varied imagined reward signals. However, on very small datasets the world model's stochastic component may collapse (KL collapse), reducing effective diversity to near zero — monitoring the KL term magnitude during training is essential.
offline_vs_online_rl_compatibility: DreamerV3 is uniquely well-suited for offline RL compared to model-free methods, because training occurs inside the world model imagination rather than requiring real environment interaction. The workflow for lottery-nn: (1) Train the RSSM world model offline on the fixed historical draw dataset (100-200 draws from draws.csv / draws_649.csv / draws_dailygrand.csv). (2) Train the Actor-Critic entirely inside the world model by generating imagined draw sequences — no new real draws are needed during Actor-Critic training. (3) After each new real draw, fine-tune the world model with the new data point and optionally re-run Actor-Critic imagination training. This is essentially a structured offline model-based RL workflow, analogous to MBPO (offline variant) or MOPO. The critical caveat is world model accuracy: an inaccurate world model trained on 100-200 draws may generate misleading imagined data, making the Actor-Critic worse than a simpler baseline. Offline model-based RL is operationally ideal (one-draw-per-week cadence) but technically risky at this data scale.
key_dependencies: PyTorch (already present). No standard DreamerV3 library is pip-installable for custom environments — the RSSM must be implemented from scratch or adapted from open-source DreamerV3 PyTorch ports. Key components: einops (tensor reshaping for RSSM), torch.distributions (Categorical, Normal for latent distributions). Optional: dreamer-pytorch (community port), mbrl-lib (Meta's MBRL library with world model components). No stable pip package for DreamerV3 as of 2025 — requires ~800-1200 lines of custom implementation.
estimated_lines_of_code: 800-1200 lines of new code: RSSM encoder/decoder (~200 lines), GRU-based dynamics model (~150 lines), stochastic latent state handling with straight-through (~100 lines), world model training loop with KL balancing, symlog, free bits (~150 lines), imagination rollout engine (~100 lines), Actor-Critic training inside imagination (~150 lines), combinatorial action adapter (autoregressive masking or top-k, ~100 lines), integration with existing SharedLotteryTransformer encoder (~80 lines, optional). This is the highest implementation complexity of any method in this research set.
transfer_learning_compatibility: Moderate compatibility with adaptation. The existing SharedLotteryTransformer encoder can serve as the RSSM observation encoder — its output embeddings replace the CNN/MLP encoder used in standard DreamerV3. Specifically: the transformer's sequence output (after processing the last SEQUENCE_LEN draws) can feed into the RSSM as the observation representation, allowing the world model to build on the pretrained feature extractor. However, the RSSM's recurrent GRU hidden state introduces a separate temporal dynamics layer that partially overlaps with the transformer's own sequence modeling, requiring careful design to avoid redundancy. The lottery_id embedding already differentiates the three lotteries, which can be passed as a conditioning signal into the RSSM dynamics. The Actor and Critic heads are new additions on top of the latent state. Recommendation: freeze the SharedLotteryTransformer encoder for world model training and only train the RSSM dynamics and decoder from scratch, using the encoder's output as fixed observation features.
specific_application_in_project: DreamerV3-style model-based RL would be applied in Phase 3 of lottery-nn, after the Phase 2 Actor-Critic baseline (REINFORCE/PPO) is established and validated. Concrete application: (1) Train an RSSM world model on each lottery's historical draw CSV (draws.csv, draws_649.csv, draws_dailygrand.csv), using the SharedLotteryTransformer encoder as the observation encoder and the lottery_id embedding for multi-lottery conditioning. (2) Generate thousands of imagined draw sequences from the RSSM, creating a synthetic augmented dataset that amplifies the 100-200 real draws. (3) Train a per-lottery Actor-Critic inside the imagination: actor outputs multi-hot logits over the ball pool (N=50 for LottoMax, N=49 for 649/DailyGrand), enforced to exactly k selections via straight-through top-k; critic estimates imagined returns using symlog and two-hot encoding. (4) At each real weekly draw: append new draw to CSV, fine-tune the world model with the new transition, re-run Actor-Critic imagination training, and generate 5 plays per lottery. (5) Reward shaping: reward = num_hits / k (range 0-1) to make the sparse lottery reward learnable inside the world model. This replaces the current temperature-softmax predict.py sampling with an Actor-Critic policy trained on imagined futures. Primary risk: world model accuracy at n=100-200; recommend validating world model prediction quality (reconstruction loss, predicted hit rate vs. actual) before committing to Phase 3 integration. Phase 2 REINFORCE baseline should be compared against the imagination-trained Actor-Critic to verify that the added complexity yields measurable improvement.
integration_point: Phase 3 (probabilistic models, DeepAR, N-BEATS) — specifically as a model-based RL augmentation that uses imagination to overcome the sample scarcity that limits Phase 2 model-free Actor-Critic methods
replaces_or_extends: Replaces temperature-softmax sampling in src/predict.py and extends the Phase 2 Actor-Critic by adding a world model (RSSM) layer between the SharedLotteryTransformer encoder and the Actor-Critic heads. The RSSM is a new component (src/world_model.py); the Actor and Critic heads from Phase 2 are reused but trained inside imagination rather than on real draw data directly.
existing_open_source_implementations: 1. danijar/dreamerv3 (https://github.com/danijar/dreamerv3) — official JAX/TensorFlow implementation by Hafner; not PyTorch-native but is the canonical reference. 2. NM512/dreamer-pytorch (https://github.com/NM512/dreamer-pytorch) — community PyTorch port of DreamerV3, reasonably complete, MIT license; most directly usable for lottery-nn integration. 3. zhaoyi11/dreamer-pytorch (https://github.com/zhaoyi11/dreamer-pytorch) — another PyTorch port with cleaner RSSM implementation. 4. facebook/mbrl-lib (https://github.com/facebookresearch/mbrl-lib) — Meta's model-based RL library with PETS, MBPO components (not DreamerV3 specifically) but provides world model primitives usable for custom RSSM. 5. google-deepmind/acme (https://github.com/google-deepmind/acme) — DeepMind's RL framework includes DreamerV2-style agents in JAX; not PyTorch. 6. No lottery-specific or combinatorial-output DreamerV3 implementation exists as of 2025 — adaptation from gym-based implementations is required.
benchmark_results: DreamerV3 (Hafner et al. 2023) key empirical results: (1) Atari 100K benchmark: DreamerV3 achieves human-normalized mean score of 1.14 with only 100K environment steps (vs. 40M for model-free PPO to reach human level) — 400x sample advantage on standard discrete action games. (2) DM Control (continuous control): DreamerV3 matches or exceeds SAC performance using 10-50x fewer environment interactions. (3) Crafter (survival game with sparse rewards): DreamerV3 achieves score 14.5% (vs. 5.3% PPO, 6.5% DreamerV2) on a task with dozens of sparse achievement signals — demonstrates robustness to reward sparsity. (4) Minecraft (open-world, extremely sparse): DreamerV3 is the first RL algorithm to obtain diamonds from scratch in Minecraft without human demonstrations — the most compelling sparse-reward result. (5) Multi-domain: A single set of hyperparameters (no tuning) works across all 7 benchmark suites, demonstrating robustness. No published DreamerV3 benchmark on combinatorial set selection (k-of-N) or offline static datasets of < 200 samples exists as of 2025.
notable_use_cases: 1. Minecraft diamond collection (Hafner et al. 2023) — extremely sparse reward (reward occurs only after 20+ sequential correct actions), structurally similar to lottery in terms of reward rarity and the need for long-horizon credit assignment. 2. Drug discovery / molecular generation — RSSM-style world models have been applied to molecule optimization with combinatorial action spaces (adding/removing atoms), providing the closest published analog to k-of-N selection with sparse reward (binding affinity measured only after full molecule is constructed). 3. Chip placement optimization (Mirhoseini et al. 2021, Nature) — combinatorial placement of circuit components using RL with imagined rollouts; demonstrates model-based RL scaling to combinatorial layout problems. 4. Offline robotics (MOPO, Kidambi et al. 2020) — world model trained on fixed offline dataset (no new environment interaction), policy optimized inside the model; most structurally analogous to the lottery-nn offline use case where real draws are fixed. 5. Game state prediction for card games (Poker, Skat) — RSSM-style models for predicting hidden state from partial observations in card games with discrete combinatorial deal distributions — moderate structural similarity to draw prediction.
